subject: True-up: Q1 usage reconciliation & one-time credit allocation
messages:
From: LedgerOps Billing <billing@ledgerops.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerops.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q1 usage report & true-up inquiry

Hi Sean,

Attached is our Q1 usage export — it looks like there was unmetered burst activity tied to a pilot project in February that pushed us ~18% over our committed throughput for the month. Our procurement team flagged the extra charge in the March invoice and asked whether Redwood can apply a one-time credit or reallocate committed units from our April renewal to cover the overage.

Can you confirm whether there is a mechanism for a retroactive true-up credit or if this needs to be handled as a one-time billable overage? We want to avoid duplicate charges during the renewal conversation next week.

Attachments: LedgerOps_Usage_Q1_2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Billing Operations | LedgerOps
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@ledgerops.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q1 usage report & true-up inquiry

Hi Daniel — thanks for sending this over and flagging ahead of your renewal. I pulled the CSV and gave it a quick pass. A couple immediate notes:

- The spike on 2026-02-18 is consistent with the pilot you mentioned (short bursts of ~4x baseline for ~8 hours).
- Usage after 02/20 looks back to normal.

Internally cc'ing Stephanie (Account Exec) and Monica (Customer Success) so we can align on the renewal cadence and the operational impact. From a billing standpoint I'll need Rafael from Finance to confirm how we handle retroactive reallocations vs. credits.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rafael and I review the usage export and produce a recommended one-time credit allocation split (e.g., % credit applied to March invoice vs. reallocation to April commit).
2) We share a short summary + adjusted invoice stub by EOD Thu so your procurement team has language for the renewal.
3) If LedgerOps prefers, we can roll the credit into the April committed units and adjust the SOW addendum prior to signing.

Is LedgerOps open to the credit being split (partial cash credit + partial commit reallocation)? If yes, please confirm who in procurement should get the invoice stub (cc Asha?).

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q1 usage report & true-up inquiry

Sean / team — I pulled the finance view. Two quick items:

1) Per our standard terms, overages are billed as one-time charges at the published rate unless we agree to apply a credit. We do have flexibility for strategic renewals to apply a one-time non-recurring credit.

2) If we reallocate committed units from April to cover March overage, we need a signed amendment or SOW addendum documenting the adjustment and revised monthly minimum, otherwise it creates a revenue recognition mismatch for our reporting.

Attached is a working worksheet with two scenarios: cash credit (full offset) and commit reallocation (partial offset + SOW addendum). My recommendation for LedgerOps (given their growth signal) is a split: 60% commit reallocation, 40% cash credit applied to the March invoice. That preserves predictable revenue while keeping the renewal path clean.

Attachments: Proposed_Credit_Allocation_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)

If that split sounds acceptable, I'll draft the invoice stub and an amendment template.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerops.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@ledgerops.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q1 usage report & true-up inquiry

Thanks all — LedgerOps is comfortable with a split solution. Procurement prefers the bulk of the offset to be reallocated to April committed units so the renewal amount stays predictable on paper; finance will accept a 40% cash credit applied to March as long as we receive a stub showing the adjusted numbers for audit.

Two asks: can Redwood provide (a) an invoice stub that applies the 40% cash credit to March and (b) an amendment to the SOW showing the April commit reallocation? If you can include a one-page summary that procurement can attach to their PO, that would speed sign-off.

If possible we'd like the stub and amendment by next Tue (10 Mar).

Best,
Asha Rao
Head of Procurement | LedgerOps
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerops.com>, Daniel Park <daniel@ledgerops.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Q1 usage report & true-up inquiry

Asha / Daniel — appreciate the quick confirmation. Rafael and I reviewed and attached the invoice stub + SOW amendment for your review. Summary of resolution:

- March invoice: apply a one-time cash credit equal to 40% of the calculated overage (line-item credit shown).
- April commit: reallocate units equal to 60% of the overage; updated monthly commit and unit pricing reflected in the SOW amendment.
- Net effect: LedgerOps receives both the March credit and the additional committed units for April; renewal PO can reference the SOW amendment.

Attachments included: Signed_SOW_Q1.pdf (PDF, 14KB) — draft amendment for countersignature; Proposed_Credit_Allocation_v2.xlsx — details; Invoice_Stub_March_2026.pdf (PDF, 6KB)

If that aligns, Monica will follow up to confirm timing for the amendment signature and update any onboarding for the reallocated capacity. Rafael will issue the credit against the March invoice once we have the countersigned amendment.

Next actions:
- Asha: please confirm the PO reference and the person who will countersign the amendment.
- LedgerOps finance: confirm the billing email to receive the adjusted invoice (if different from billing@ledgerops.com).

Thanks — we’ll aim to have the adjustment captured before your renewal close next week.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
